title: Admin export design review - Cygnus Retail
summary: Redwood reviewed admin and security event capture, export mechanisms (S3, Splunk HEC, Kafka, webhooks), retention controls, KMS/HSM BYOK options, redaction transforms, replay windows, and region pinning for data residency. Customer prefers immutable archival to their Splunk/S3 pipeline with on-platform 90-day retention and long-term off-platform storage. Follow-up items include sample schema, architecture diagram for VPC egress, egress IPs, and a POC checklist.
topics: Export mechanisms: S3, Splunk HEC, Kafka, webhooks
next_steps: Redwood to share sample admin-audit JSON schema and example event stream by 2025-12-02
Customer to confirm preferred export target (Splunk on-prem vs BigQuery) and egress firewall rules by 2025-12-05
Schedule 30-min POC to validate S3+Glue export and KMS integration week of 2025-12-08
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share export schema and presigned S3 put example; due 2025-12-02
Priya Shah: Prepare architecture diagram for VPC egress and HSM/KMS flow; due 2025-12-03
Ethan Park: Confirm Splunk index name and firewall egress IPs; due 2025-12-05
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-28 15:00 PST - Duration: 43m. Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CISO, Cygnus), Ethan Park (Head of Platform), Leah O'Connor (Compliance)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. We'll do a quick run-through on admin activity capture and export options, then zoom into KMS and retention. Priya will cover the schema and wire-up.
[00:22] Marta Ruiz: Great, high level - our auditors want an immutable stream of admin events to land in our Splunk cluster, and we'll need on-platform retention capped at 90 days for PII reasons.
[00:35] Priya Shah: Ok that makes sense. Quick note, our platform captures system level admin events, user-level actions, role changes, token and API key operations, workspace and model changes, policy updates, and console logins. We also surface SAML/SCIM provisioning events separately.
[00:55] Ethan Park: When you say captures, is that both UI and API? Like if a script rotates keys via API, will that be in the same stream?
[01:08] Priya Shah: Yes, both UI and API. Events are normalized to the same schema - there's an actor, action, target, timestamp, request-id and raw-payload. Sometimes the transcript shows 'kay vee cache' but it's KV cache in the payload - apologies for typos.
[01:30] Leah O'Connor: Can you show an example event? We need to see fields that map to SOC 2 evidence.
[01:40] Priya Shah: Sure - high-level example: {event_type: 'admin.change_role', actor: {id:'u-123', email:'...'}, target: {type:'role', id:'r-45'}, timestamp: '2025-11-28T22:39:12Z', request_id: 'req-...', detail: {before:'viewer', after:'admin'}} - we'll send a more complete JSON.
[02:10] Marta Ruiz: For immutability, can we get a signed append-only S3 bucket or Kafka stream with server-side immutability?
[02:20] Jordan Lee: We support pushing events to S3 (gzip'd newline delimited JSON), webhook endpoints, Kafka, and partners like Splunk HEC. For S3 we can do presigned uploads and you can enforce bucket settings (object lock) on your side. For strict immutability use S3 retention/LEGAL-HOLD policies.
[02:45] Ethan Park: Does Redwood support pushing directly into our on-prem Splunk or does it require a relay?
[02:52] Priya Shah: We can deliver via Splunk HEC over TLS. If you have strict egress rules, we'd recommend a small relay VM in your VPC that accepts the push and forwards internally. We also support a pull model - you can pull from presigned S3 objects.
[03:12] Leah O'Connor: What's the delivery guarantee? At-least-once or exactly-once?
[03:18] Priya Shah: Currently at-least-once semantics - we include idempotency keys at the event level so consumers can dedupe. For Kafka we can get closer to exactly-once with consumer dedupe.
[03:35] Marta Ruiz: KMS - we need BYOK and HSM-backed keys. How does Redwood integrate?
[03:44] Jordan Lee: Two modes: customer-managed keys in cloud KMS for envelope encryption of stored exports, and HSM-backed option for Private deployments where keys never leave your HSM. For hosted customers we integrate with your KMS via IAM role grants.
[04:05] Ethan Park: Key rotation - how often and who rotates? Also audit trail of key usage for SOC 2.
[04:13] Priya Shah: Key rotation can be managed by you; we recommend 90-180 day cadence. KMS usage is logged in CloudTrail; Redwood's admin event stream will include key-association events (key-id used, key-version).
[04:35] Leah O'Connor: Data residency - our EU admin events need to stay in eu-west-1 for 400 days. Does Redwood have region pinning?
[04:47] Jordan Lee: Yes, region pinning for logs and serving. Exports can be routed to region-local storage; hosted tenants can be set to a default region.
[05:10] Marta Ruiz: Retention control - on-platform 90 days and exported copy for 7 years off-platform, supported?
[05:20] Priya Shah: Yes - on-platform retention configurable per-org/workspace; exported copies you control and can retain as required.
[05:40] Ethan Park: Any UX for deleting PII from stored events?
[05:52] Priya Shah: We have redaction rules. Default raw payload may include usernames/emails; we can configure field-level redaction (hashing or removal) prior to export. For SOC 2 evidence you often want actor id, not email, so hashing and mapping tables work.
[06:15] Marta Ruiz: Can we get signed audit proofs? Like chain-of-trust?
[06:22] Jordan Lee: We can support event signing - HMAC per batch and verification keys. Combine with S3 object-lock for tamper-evidence.
[06:40] Leah O'Connor: RBAC and SSO logging - include SAML assertion metadata?
[06:52] Priya Shah: We capture SSO events and can attach SAML assertion IDs; we don't capture full assertion by default but can store IDs and metadata. SCIM provisioning events include before/after.
[07:10] Ethan Park: How noisy is the stream? We don't want chatty telemetry.
[07:20] Priya Shah: Event categories: admin, system, telemetry. Admin events are lower volume and are included by default. Telemetry enabled separately.
[07:40] Jordan Lee: We have batching - default per-minute S3 batches to reduce requests; Splunk HEC streams continuously.
[08:05] [screen share - Priya pastes sample schema]
[08:12] Priya Shah: Sample for 'api.key.rotate' includes actor.id, actor.role, object.id, previous_key_fingerprint, new_key_fingerprint (fingerprints only), timestamp, request_id, source_ip. Full schema in follow-up.
[08:40] Marta Ruiz: Is request-id traceable to model invocation?
[08:50] Priya Shah: We include correlation ids where available; model change events include model id and inference request ids when applicable, occasional gaps with third-party connectors.
[09:10] Ethan Park: For on-prem private deploy - how does export egress work with strict firewall?
[09:18] Jordan Lee: Private deployments can have an egress gateway in your network. Redwood control plane hands off events to a local collector agent which writes to local storage or forwards to internal bus; agent can use your HSM.
[09:39] Leah O'Connor: Console session logs - IPs, MFA success/failure?
[09:47] Priya Shah: Yes, console login events include IP, user-agent, MFA result, and suspicious login flags.
[10:05] Marta Ruiz: Map Redwood events to our SOC 2 evidence YAML?
[10:12] Jordan Lee: We can produce a mapping sheet linking event types to SOC 2 control IDs. Priya will include starter mapping.
[10:25] Ethan Park: Are export payloads compressed and signed?
[10:29] Priya Shah: S3 exports gzip compressed and optionally HMAC signed per file. Webhooks over HEC use TLS and support HMAC headers.
[10:45] Marta Ruiz: Replay window if we miss events?
[10:52] Priya Shah: Short replay window - default 30 days for hosted customers. For durability use S3 exports as source of truth.
[11:12] Ethan Park: Scale - recommended ingestion patterns for Splunk?
[11:22] Priya Shah: Best practice: batched S3 -> Splunk ingestion or Splunk HEC with batching on the relay, idempotency keys and partition by date/workspace.
[11:45] Jordan Lee: Any compliance certs we should note?
[11:53] Marta Ruiz: We're SOC 2 Type II in process and ISO scoping next year.
[12:02] Priya Shah: We'll provide SOC 2 evidence pack guidance.
[12:18] Leah O'Connor: We need to filter exports so PII never leaves for less-trusted sinks - mask emails when pushing to BigQuery.
[12:30] Priya Shah: Per-destination transform pipeline supported. For BigQuery run transform job before upload; for Splunk apply transforms on the relay.
[12:50] Ethan Park: Can we keep only hash in exported events while full detail on-platform for 90 days?
[13:00] Priya Shah: Yes - supported config: full detail on-platform N days, sanitized export to external sinks.
[13:20] Marta Ruiz: Incident response - streaming alerts for suspicious admin activity?
[13:28] Jordan Lee: We can send alert webhooks and create tickets in Jira/ServiceNow; also emit high-priority events with higher retention.
[13:45] Leah O'Connor: Tamper-evident chain for infra changes - HSM + object-lock enough?
[13:53] Priya Shah: Recommended combined approach: sign batches with HMAC, push to S3 with object-lock, mirror to immutable store.
[14:10] Ethan Park: How do you rotate signing keys and verify old archives?
[14:15] Priya Shah: Recommend key rotation schedule and include key-version metadata with each batch; preserve verification keys to verify archives.
[14:35] Jordan Lee: Blockers for Splunk HEC vs S3?
[14:42] Marta Ruiz: HEC preferable for near-real-time, security prefers S3 for immutability. Both can be used: S3 archival + HEC for alerts.
[15:00] Priya Shah: Pattern common - S3 for archival, HEC for real-time; support both simultaneously.
[15:20] Ethan Park: Need egress IP ranges.
[15:24] Jordan Lee: We'll provide Redwood egress IPs or agent IP for VPC mode.
[15:40] Leah O'Connor: SCIM provisioning diffs?
[15:48] Priya Shah: Provisioning events include before/after diffs.
[16:05] Marta Ruiz: Can you provide a 30-day sample export for ingestion test?
[16:12] Jordan Lee: Yes - we'll generate a redacted sample with realistic volumes and schema.
[16:28] [customer asks about GDPR right to be forgotten and audit evidence]
[16:33] Priya Shah: We support expunging PII on request and keep a minimal audit stub indicating deletion happened for evidence without returning PII.
[16:50] Ethan Park: Role definition versioning?
[16:56] Priya Shah: Role definitions versioned; role-change events include prior and new definition snapshot id.
[17:12] Marta Ruiz: Include Terraform plan id when infra changes via IaC?
[17:18] Priya Shah: We accept correlation id in API payload - pass plan id and it will be forwarded in event.
[17:40] Jordan Lee: We'll add SOC 2 CC6/CC7 mapping in follow-up doc.
[17:50] Leah O'Connor: Do you support mTLS for webhook deliveries?
[17:58] Priya Shah: Yes - client cert mTLS supported for high-assurance endpoints.
[18:12] Ethan Park: Size limits per event/batch?
[18:18] Priya Shah: Per-event payload limit ~256KB; recommend 100MB gzip chunks per S3 file.
[18:35] Marta Ruiz: Retention proof and deletion logs to auditors?
[18:42] Jordan Lee: We can provide retention config snapshots and deletion events in the admin stream as evidence.
[19:00] [brief pause - team notes action items]
[19:20] Ethan Park: Where configure pipelines - Console or API?
[19:28] Priya Shah: Both. Console wizard for common sinks; API endpoints for automation.
[19:48] Jordan Lee: Alerts on export failures?
[19:52] Priya Shah: We emit delivery_failed events and will retry; alerts to PagerDuty/Slack supported.
[20:10] Marta Ruiz: BigQuery limitations?
[20:18] Priya Shah: Support schema registry for BigQuery; fields stable and new fields nullable to avoid drift.
[20:38] Leah O'Connor: Who at Redwood can view admin events?
[20:45] Jordan Lee: Access is role-based; only authorized Redwood SRE/ops on need-to-know have access. In Dedicated/Private you can lock Redwood out entirely.
[21:02] Ethan Park: SLA around export latency?
[21:07] Priya Shah: HEC streaming sub-second to second, S3 batched 60-90s typical; SLA varies.
[21:28] Marta Ruiz: Include minimal compliance checklist for auditors in follow-up.
[21:36] Jordan Lee: Will do.
[21:45] [customer asks about retention policy change history]
[21:50] Priya Shah: Platform records retention policy changes as admin events.
[22:10] Ethan Park: For private deployments, sequence for key provisioning into HSM?
[22:18] Priya Shah: Key generated inside HSM, store only key references, derive envelope keys.
[22:40] Marta Ruiz: Legal hold handling?
[22:46] Jordan Lee: Tag event batches with legal-hold metadata and Redwood will not purge until release; exports include hold flag.
[23:05] Leah O'Connor: Cross-account S3 writes gotchas?
[23:10] Priya Shah: Need proper bucket policies and IAM roles for presigned uploads; we'll provide example trust policy.
[23:30] Jordan Lee: Recap time.
[23:35] Marta Ruiz: Recap: sample schema, S3 archival + Splunk HEC real-time, object-lock suggestion, KMS BYOK + HSM option, redaction options, replay window and retention mapping for SOC 2.
[23:52] Jordan Lee: We'll send sample JSON, architecture diagram, egress IPs, SOC 2 mapping table.
[24:05] Priya Shah: I'll include a POC checklist - what to enable, firewall rules, sample ingest steps for Splunk.
[24:20] Ethan Park: We'll decide S3 vs HEC by Friday.
[24:30] Leah O'Connor: Do you capture who exported logs?
[24:36] Priya Shah: Yes - export actions are admin events themselves.
[24:50] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. Follow-ups as discussed.

End of call.

Transcript notes: automatic transcription, occasional mis-heard acronyms (KMS as K-M-S, 'kay vee cache' for KV cache), timestamps approximate.
